geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Ladder and wall problem.

Goal: I can define and use sine and cosine.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
sin A = opposite/hypotenuse and cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse.

A memory aid is SOH CAH TOA. Since the hypotenuse is the longest side, sine and cosine of an acute angle are between 0 and 1.

The acute angles of a right triangle are complementary, and the side opposite one is adjacent to the other, so sin A = cos(90 − A). A 6 m ladder leaning at 70 degrees to the ground reaches 6 sin 70 degrees, about 5.64 m, up the wall, and its foot is 6 cos 70 degrees, about 2.05 m, from the wall.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: If sin A = 0.6 in a right triangle, what is cos(90 − A)? Find cos A.
slides.reveal: cos(90 − A) = 0.6. With hypotenuse 5 and opposite 3, the adjacent leg is 4, so cos A = 0.8.
